title: Paragliding Apps: From Forecast to Flight Analysis
content:
## A Pilot's Workflow Guide for the Dales Club

**(Your Name Here)**
**(Date)**
notes: Opening slide. Introduce yourself and the topic.

title: Introduction - The Timeline Approach
content:
*   **Goal:** Navigate the complex world of paragliding apps relevant to Dales Club pilots.
*   **Structure:** We'll follow a timeline, from planning at home to post-flight analysis.
*   **Focus:** Key apps used at each stage, highlighting personal recommendations and common practices within the club context. Suitable for all levels, especially those aspiring to XC.
*   **Disclaimer:** App landscape changes constantly! This reflects current practices (March 2025).
*   **Interaction:** Please ask questions as we go!
notes: Set the stage, explain the workflow approach, manage expectations about changing tech, encourage questions.

title: Phase 1: Pre-Flight Planning (At Home/Work)
content:
*   **Context:** Got internet, computer/phone, time to research before a potential flying day.
*   **Key Activities:**
    *   Weather Forecasting (Is it flyable? Is it XC potential?)
    *   Site Research (Viability, access, characteristics)
    *   Reviewing past flights (yours and others on XContest etc.)
    *   Getting initial ideas for sites/routes.
*   **Primary Tools Discussed:**
    *   Windy
    *   Lazy RASP
    *   Social Channels (Initial checks - Dales Flying Plans etc.)
    *   Met Office / UKV (via Windy)
notes: Introduce the first phase of the pilot workflow - planning and the initial set of tools used.

title: Deep Dive: Windy
content:
*   **Overview:** Powerful, visual weather forecasting tool. Freemium model.
    *   Website: [https://www.windy.com](https://www.windy.com)
*   **Free vs. Premium:**
    *   Free: 3-hourly forecast intervals. Still very useful for initial checks.
    *   Premium (Highly Recommended): ~£2/month. *Primary benefit: 1-hourly forecast intervals.* Essential for detailed planning. Also more forecast updates, longer outlooks/loops. Well worth the cost (less than 1/3 tank of fuel/year!).
*   **Key Models:** Access multiple global and high-resolution models.
    *   **ECMWF:** High-quality European model (often default).
    *   **GFS:** US Global model (lower resolution, free, basis for RASP).
    *   **UKV:** UK Met Office high-resolution model (often most accurate for UK). **The go-to for detailed UK forecasts.**
    *   ICON, AROME, etc. available for comparison.
*   **Focus:** Use UKV primarily, check ECMWF/others for agreement = higher confidence.
notes: Introduce Windy as the primary forecasting tool. Emphasize the value of Premium and the importance of the UKV model for UK flying.

title: Windy Features
content:
*   **Layers:** Visualize key parameters: Wind (altitudes), Gusts, Clouds (base/levels), Rain, Thermals (CAPE/Lift), Temperature, Radar & Satellite etc. Crucial for understanding the day.
*   **Model Comparison View:** Side-by-side forecasts for a point/time. **Use this!** High agreement = more confidence. GFS disagreeing widely? Distrust GFS & RASP for that day.
*   **Soundings (Advanced):** Vertical atmospheric profile. Good for deeper dive into stability, inversion layers, thermal strength/height. More useful for experienced XC pilots.
*   **Point Forecasts:** Detailed meteograms/airgrams for specific sites.
*   **Webcams & Spots:** Integrated map for quick checks.
notes: Highlight the key features within Windy that pilots use - Layers, Model Comparison, Soundings etc. Emphasize using the comparison view.

title: Understanding RASP
content:
*   **What is RASP?** Regional Atmospheric Soaring Prediction.
    *   *Soaring specific* model enhancement, usually based on **GFS**.
*   **Characteristics:** Community-driven, complex, older tech. Unlikely to improve significantly.
*   **Key Limitation:** **Garbage In, Garbage Out.** If GFS forecast is wrong, RASP will be wrong. *Always cross-reference with Windy (UKV/ECMWF)!*
*   **Common Use:** Quick look for "Star Rating" (XC potential 0-5) and Wind overview via simpler interfaces.
*   **Star Ratings:** 0 = likely unflyable/no lift, 5 = potential good XC day. Foot Launch stars are more conservative on wind.
notes: Explain what RASP is, its GFS dependency, and its limitations. Manage expectations about its accuracy and stress verification.

title: Accessing RASP Data (UK Examples)
content:
*   **1. Lazy RASP:**
    *   Simplified web view for quick weekly overview (Stars, Wind).
    *   Good for spotting *potential* days. *Requires verification* with Windy.
    *   Link: (e.g., `lazyrasp.com` - confirm specific URL used locally)
*   **2. Stratus RASP:**
    *   Most detailed RASP interface (best on desktop). For deep dives into all parameters. Steeper learning curve.
    *   Link: [http://rasp.stratus.org.uk/](http://rasp.stratus.org.uk/)
*   **3. XC Power RASP:**
    *   Mobile-friendly interface with Google Maps background. Simplified parameters. Good compromise for phone checks.
    *   Link: (e.g., `xcpara.co.uk` - confirm specific URL used locally)
notes: Show the different ways pilots typically access RASP data, highlighting the pros and cons of each interface.

title: Other Forecasting & Site Tools
content:
*   **1. Flybubble Weather:**
    *   Combines RASP data (Stars, Wind) with site database (Paragliding Earth). Green/Red blobs for potential site flyability.
    *   **Pros:** Good for *generating ideas* of where might work based *only* on RASP.
    *   **Cons/Caveats:**
        *   **Relies solely on RASP** (Discard if RASP looks wrong via Windy).
        *   Site wind tolerances can be **very inaccurate** (e.g., shows Semerwater flyable in NNE). *Your site knowledge is essential.* Treat as idea generator only.
    *   Link: [https://flybubble.com/weather](https://flybubble.com/weather)
*   **2. Paragliding Map:**
    *   Global site database + basic forecast (Windfinder?). Smiley faces for *current* flyability (paid for future).
    *   **Pros:** Useful site database reference.
    *   **Cons:** Forecast source unclear, optimized for mountains (can show flyable in zero wind - bad for Dales!), uses Paragliding Earth data. Less useful for planning.
    *   Link: [https://paraglidingmap.com](https://paraglidingmap.com)
*   **3. Paragliding Earth:**
    *   The *underlying database* for many site maps. Raw site info (coordinates, descriptions).
    *   Link: [https://paraglidingearth.com](https://paraglidingearth.com)
notes: Discuss supplementary tools, emphasizing their specific uses and MAJOR caveats (especially Flybubble's RASP reliance and inaccurate tolerances).

title: Phase 2: Social Coordination & Final Checks
content:
*   **Context:** Forecast looks promising, sites identified. Time to collaborate. Usually evening before / morning of.
*   **Key Activities:** Discussing forecast/sites, sharing screenshots, leveraging collective knowledge, making plans, CANP.
*   **Primary Tools:** **Telegram Groups**, CANP System.
notes: Transition to the coordination phase. Highlight the importance of teamwork and introduce the tools used.

title: Social Channels (Dales Club Context)
content:
*   **Value of Teamwork:** Forecasting is hard! Multiple eyes, different perspectives (weather nerds, local gurus, experienced XC pilots) improve decisions.
*   **Dales Groups (Telegram):**
    *   **Flying Plans:** General chat for all.
    *   **Progress:** Aimed at newer pilots focusing on site flying, ridge soaring, first thermals.
    *   **10/100:** Focus on XC - planning, flying together, retrieve. The primary group for XC discussions.
*   **Best Practice:**
    *   Do *your own* initial research (Windy!).
    *   Post *ideas* with screenshots & specific questions. "What do folk think of Stags Fell tomorrow based on this UKV? Looks marginal NE early?"
    *   If no replies, re-check basics (Rain? Too windy?). Maybe the idea needs refining.
*   **Outcome:** Better plans, shared understanding, flying buddies, safer flying.
notes: Explain the role of club Telegram groups, referencing specific Dales groups. Emphasize best practices for effective communication.

title: Pre-Flight Admin: CANP
content:
*   **What:** Civil Aircraft Notification Procedure.
*   **Purpose:** Notify primarily **midweek** air traffic (Military low flying, increasingly others via NOTAM) of planned gliding activity.
*   **Why:** Safety! Makes low-flying aircraft aware of your potential presence. Creates temporary advisory area (2nm radius, up to 2000ft AGL).
*   **How:**
    *   **Recommended:** Online/App (`canp.logans.me.uk`, BHPA links). Faster.
    *   Need: Site (name/grid ref), Date, Times (local), Activity, Altitude (AMSL), Contact.
*   **When:** Submit by 8pm evening before (Mon-Thurs), 3pm Fri for weekend/Mon.
*   **Tactics:** Can notify for launch site, or potential XC area downwind.
*   **Links:** [BHPA CANP Info](https://www.bhpa.co.uk/members/safety/canp/) , [CANP for Fliers App Info](https://www.bhpa.co.uk/members/safety/canp-for-free-fliers-app/)
notes: Explain the CANP system - what it is, why it's important (especially midweek), how and when to submit.

title: Phase 3: XC Planning (Optional but Recommended)
content:
*   **Context:** Aiming to fly XC. Even short XC flights benefit from planning.
*   **Why Plan?** Understand airspace, identify landing/retrieve options (roads, rail), have a goal, share route with others.
*   **Beginner XC:** Follow experienced pilots! Get *their* route QR code into your instrument. Provides a line, helps you follow, learn sensible routes.
*   **Tools:** Fly XC, Northern Challenge Series tasks, Open Railway Map.
notes: Introduce XC planning. Explain why it's beneficial even for beginners and highlight the value of following experienced pilots' routes.

title: XC Planning Tools
content:
*   **1. Fly XC:**
    *   Web-based tool. Easy to use.
    *   Draw routes, view airspace, add waypoints, export (GPX, KML, instrument formats), **generate QR codes** for easy sharing via phone. **This is the go-to.**
    *   Link: [https://flyxc.app/](https://flyxc.app/)
*   **2. Northern Challenge Series:**
    *   Pre-defined tasks used in local friendly competitions.
    *   Excellent for practice even if not competing. Program into your instrument for navigation practice on the hill. Find tasks on NCS website/forums.
    *   Link: (Search for Northern Challenge Series Paragliding)
*   **3. Open Railway Map:**
    *   Map focused *only* on railway lines/stations. Quickly identify retrieve options near potential XC routes.
    *   Link: [https://www.openrailwaymap.org/](https://www.openrailwaymap.org/)
notes: Detail the primary tools used for XC planning: FlyXC (emphasize QR codes), NCS tasks for practice, and Open Railway Map for retrieve points.

title: Phase 4: Going Flying (Tracking & In-Flight)
content:
*   **Context:** On the hill, during the flight.
*   **Importance of Location Sharing & In-Flight Data:**
    *   **Safety & Retrieve:** Essential for ground crews / buddies to know your location.
    *   **In-Flight Coordination:** Seeing other pilots on flight instruments (live tracking, FLARM).
    *   **Navigation & Airspace:** Using flight computers effectively.
*   **Key Tools:** **XCTrack/FlySkyHy**, PURETRACK (aggregator), XContest Live, Google Maps (ground), FLARM/OGN.
notes: Move to the actual flying phase. Stress the importance of tracking for safety/retrieve and introduce the key in-flight tools.

title: In-Flight App: XCTrack (Android)
content:
*   **Overview:** The dominant free flight computer app for Android. Hugely powerful & configurable.
*   **Key Features:**
    *   **GPS Navigation:** Shows map, waypoints, planned route, airspace.
    *   **Vario:** Audible/visual indication of lift/sink (using phone sensors or external Bluetooth vario).
    *   **Flight Data:** Ground speed, Altitude (GPS/Barometric), Wind speed/direction (calculated), Glide ratio, Distances, etc.
    *   **Airspace Warnings:** Visual and audible alerts for nearby/upcoming airspace. Essential for XC.
    *   **Live Tracking:** Uploads your position to XContest Live (feeds PURETRACK etc.). **Configure this!**
    *   **Buddy Tracking:** Can display positions of other pilots who are live tracking (via XContest/PURETRACK feed).
    *   **Task Navigation:** Follow pre-programmed routes (XC, competition tasks).
    *   **Customizable Screens:** Configure multiple pages showing the info you need.
*   **Learning Curve:** Can seem complex initially, but essential tool for XC progression. Start simple, add complexity later. Lots of online guides/tutorials.
*   **Link:** [https://xctrack.org/](https://xctrack.org/) (Also on Google Play Store)
notes: Deep dive into XCTrack. Cover its core functionalities, emphasizing airspace, live tracking, and buddy tracking. Acknowledge the learning curve.

title: In-Flight App: FlySkyHy (iOS)
content:
*   **Overview:** The main equivalent of XCTrack for iPhone/iPad users.
*   **Features:** Generally aims for feature parity with XCTrack:
    *   GPS Navigation, Maps, Vario, Flight Data, Airspace, Live Tracking, Buddy Viewing, Task Navigation.
*   **Caveats (Based on user reports):**
    *   Often requires **in-app purchases** for different modules (e.g., advanced maps, airspace, live tracking features) to match full XCTrack functionality. Can add up.
    *   Check current version/pricing for features like XContest live tracking and buddy viewing.
*   **Recommendation:** If you use iOS, this is likely your best option, but be prepared for potential costs for full XC features.
*   **Link:** (Search on Apple App Store)
notes: Cover FlySkyHy as the iOS alternative. Mention feature parity goals but highlight the common need for in-app purchases based on user feedback.

title: Tracking: Ground vs. Air Summary
content:
*   **1. Ground Tracking (Persistent Location - For Retrieve):**
    *   **Recommended: Google Maps Location Sharing** (Reliable, integrates with nav, easy). Share with retrieve drivers / trusted buddies.
*   **2. Flight Tracking (Live Flight Data - For Flying):**
    *   **Apps (XCTrack/FlySkyHy):** Configure to upload to **XContest Live Tracking**.
    *   **PURETRACK (Aggregator):** The platform aiming to show *everyone* (XContest, FLARM, Satellite). Good place for spectators/retrieve to watch. Link: [https://puretrack.io/](https://puretrack.io/)
    *   **FLARM/OGN:** Dedicated devices for local awareness (seeing/being seen by gliders etc.). Important for busy airfields / alpine flying. Some integrated into varios (e.g., Skytraxx).
    *   **Satellite Trackers (InReach/SPOT):** Global coverage, feed into PURETRACK etc. Good for remote areas.
*   **Goal:** Be visible on Google Maps (ground) AND PURETRACK/XContest (air).
notes: Summarize the two types of tracking needed: Google Maps for ground/retrieve, and flight tracking (XContest/PURETRACK etc.) for air visibility. Mention FLARM/Satellite.

title: Phase 5: Post-Flight (Landing & Retrieve)
content:
*   **Context:** Landed safely (hopefully XC!).
*   **Immediate Actions:** Pack wing safely, **upload tracklog** from XCTrack/FlySkyHy to XContest. **Communicate landing** on Telegram (10/100 group, Retrieve group) with **Google Maps location pin**.
*   **Retrieve Coordination:**
    *   Use Dales retrieve groups (Telegram). Share Google Maps live location. Check group for who is driving/closest.
    *   Use Google Maps for public transport or guiding driver. Open Railway Map for quick station checks.
*   **Hitching:** Use maps for direction. Location sharing helps monitor progress.
*   **XC Retrieve System:** Web system around LiveTrack24. Less used now, but commands (`/map`) exist in some groups. Telegram groups + Google Maps are more common.
notes: Outline the steps after landing: immediate actions (upload, communicate), and retrieve coordination using Telegram and Google Maps primarily. Briefly mention XC Retrieve system.

title: Phase 6: Post-Flight Analysis & Logging (Back Home)
content:
*   **Context:** Back home, review flight, log it, learn, share.
*   **Key Activities:** Analyse track, visualize, log for personal records / XC League, share experience on Club Forum, look at others' flights.
*   **Tools:** XContest, Ayvri/SportsTrackLive, Dales Club Forum, IGC Analysis Software (XC Analytics), UK XC League.
notes: Introduce the final phase - what to do after the flying day is over. Focus on analysis, logging, and sharing.

title: Analysis & Logging Tools
content:
*   **1. XContest:** Primary platform for viewing flights (yours and others). Filter by date/location. Analyse stats. Link: [https://www.xcontest.org/uk/](https://www.xcontest.org/uk/)
*   **2. 3D Visualisation:**
    *   **Ayvri:** Popular online 3D replay. Sync with video. Free/Pro tiers. Link: [https://ayvri.com/](https://ayvri.com/)
    *   **SportsTrackLive:** Alternative platform with 3D replay. Link: [https://sportstracklive.com/](https://sportstracklive.com/)
*   **3. Dales Club Forum:** **Highly Recommended!**
    *   Write up your flight! Share insights, photos, learnings.
    *   Search finds your old posts = effective personal logbook + club contribution.
    *   Link: (Provide specific club forum link)
*   **4. IGC Analysis Software:**
    *   **XC Analytics:** Excellent online tool for detailed IGC file analysis (thermal strength/drift, route choices, efficiency etc.). Great for learning. Link: [https://xcanalytics.fr/en/](https://xcanalytics.fr/en/)
    *   *Others:* SeeYou (Paid Desktop), ParaTrack (Free Online), GPSDump (Free Desktop).
*   **5. UK XC League:** National / Club online leagues via XContest. Check latest entries (submission order). Free Club League entry. Link: (Search UK XC League)
notes: Detail the specific tools for analysis and logging: XContest, 3D viewers, the crucial role of the Club Forum, XC Analytics for deep dives, and the XC League.

title: Summary & Key Takeaways
content:
*   **Workflow:** Plan (Windy/UKV) -> Coordinate (Telegram) -> Fly (XCTrack/FlySkyHy + Live Track) -> Retrieve (Google Maps/Telegram) -> Analyse (XContest/XC Analytics/Forum).
*   **Forecasting:** **Windy Premium + UKV** primary. Verify RASP. Cross-reference models.
*   **In-Flight:** **XCTrack/FlySkyHy** essential for XC nav, airspace, vario, live tracking.
*   **Tracking:** **Google Maps** (ground) + **XContest Live** via app (feeding **PURETRACK**) (air).
*   **Logging:** **XContest** upload + **Dales Club Forum** write-up = great logbook.
*   **Community:** Leverage club **Telegram groups** for planning & retrieve.
notes: Summarize the entire workflow and reinforce the key tool recommendations for each stage.
